newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee nuke confirms possible summer restart.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee nuke confirms possible summer restart.

text.p: Maine Yankee confirmed Thursday its 910 megawatt nuclear power plant could resume operations this summer following the replacement of fuel assemblies.
The company plans to replace 92 fuel assemblies immediately, including 68 fuel assemblies placed in the reactor vessel in 1995, Maine Yankee said in a statement.
Another 24 fuel assemblies will be replaced to ensure the plant can complete a typical 18-month operating cycle before going through its next refueling outage, the company said.

The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said earlier Thursday in its daily plant status report that Maine Yankee, located in Wiscasset, Maine, could restart in August following the fuel bundle replacement.

"Maine Yankee has decided to replace 68 questionable fuel assemblies now rather than wait until the scheduled fall refueling, effectively launching several outage projects seven months early," Maine Yankee said in the statement.

The company said it has determined its most recent load of fuel is unacceptable for continued operations, and said the fuel supplier is expected to submit a proposal for replacement of the fuel under contract warranty provisions.

Other work previously scheduled for the fall refueling outage will be completed, including an inspection of the plant's three steam generators and upgrades identified in an independent safety assessment, the company said.
The NRC placed Maine Yankee on its watchlist in late January following a series of unplanned outages over the past two years.
The plant was shut December 6 to correct electrical cable problems.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
